proverb: A little knowledge is a dangerous thing
meaning: A small amount of knowledge can mislead people into thinking they are more expert than they really are.
example: He read one article about first aid and tried to treat a broken arm himself. A little knowledge is a dangerous thing.

meaning: Indecision or delay in critical moments can lead to missed opportunities or failure.
example: She thought about the job offer for so long that someone else took it. He who hesitates is lost.

proverb: Make hay while the sun shines
meaning: Take advantage of an opportunity while you still can.
example: The shop is having a sale this weekend only, so make hay while the sun shines!

proverb: Good things come to those who wait
example: I waited a year for the new game to come out, and it was worth it. Good things come to those who wait.

proverb: A stitch in time saves nine
meaning: Fixing a small problem early prevents it from becoming a much bigger one.
example: Repair the leak now. A stitch in time saves nine.

meaning: What people do is a better sign of their intentions than what they say.
example: He promised to help, but never showed up. Actions speak louder than words.

meaning: It is better to do something late than not to do it at all.
example: I finally finished my homework at midnight, but better late than never.

proverb: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
meaning: Do not rely on something good happening until it has actually happened.
example: You haven't got the job yet, so don't count your chickens before they hatch.

meaning: Check that something is not going to cause problems or have a bad result before you do it.
example: Before you sign the contract, read it carefully. Look before you leap.

meaning: Doing what is morally right is rewarding in itself, even if you receive no external reward or recognition.
example: He returned the lost wallet and asked for nothing. Virtue is its own reward.

meaning: A task is soon accomplished if several people help.
example: The whole class helped clean the room, and it took ten minutes. Many hands make light work.

meaning: Repeated effort and consistent practice lead to improvement and eventual mastery.
example: She played the song every day until she got it right. Practise makes perfect.

meaning: People who take bold risks are more likely to succeed than those who hold back.
example: She spoke to the director about her idea and got the job. Fortune favors the bold.

meaning: It's wiser to be cautious and careful than to be hasty or rash and so do something you may later regret.
example: Take an umbrella, just in case. Better safe than sorry.
